GM Automation

Ugmuls 5.5e Automation connects Foundry’s chat cards, map, and combat tracker. Players roll and react from chat. GMs choose what runs automatically and can step in to correct or resolve an action.

Simple Combat Cards

A typical weapon strike posts three cards in Foundry. Simple Combat Cards groups the weapon use, attack roll, and damage roll into one card that updates as the action resolves. The card shows the target, attack result, and damage together, without repeating the item and action details across separate messages.

Base Foundry 3 cards

  1. Weapon use
  2. Attack roll
  3. Damage roll

Simple Combat Cards 1 card

  1. Weapon use
  2. Attack roll
  3. Damage roll

With Smart Reactions enabled, the action pauses when a choice can change the outcome. Shield can change a hit before damage rolls, while Parry waits until the damage is visible. Once players use or decline their options, the same card grows to show the next roll, effect, or application control as needed.

The GM can take over a pending save or use Apply and Undo from the card. Supported roll corrections preserve the original dice.

Saving throws, healing, and temporary HP can also use grouped cards. See examples from play.

Smart Reactions

With Smart Automation enabled, chat pauses when an eligible feature can change the outcome. Counterspell can interrupt a cast, Shield can answer a hit, and Parry can reduce damage after the player sees the roll.

Players use or decline their own choices. The GM can clear the remaining choices with Decline Reaction to continue the action. Configure the pauses under Module Options → Reaction Triggers.

Region Automation

Place a supported spell area on the map and let its Region handle saves, damage, or conditions when creatures enter, move through, or start or end a turn inside. Attached areas such as Spirit Guardians move with their source, and linked Regions can clear when concentration ends.

Use the Spell and Region Manager to review, edit, or disable trigger recipes.

Targeting Assist

Preview who an area will affect before placing it. Supported activities use their targeting rules to include allies, enemies, or all eligible creatures. When a spell asks you to select targets, confirm who is included before rolling.

Use Retarget on the card to correct its recorded targets. If damage has already been applied, undo it before correcting and reapplying.

Repeat Effects

Automated Effects follows up on supported conditions and monster abilities. It can offer an escape check for a grapple, prompt another save against poison, or roll recurring damage on the configured turn. The follow-up keeps the original source and save DC.

GMs can enable, edit, or add recipes for configured effects and their native activities.

Monster and Paladin Auras

Supported monster auras, such as fear and stench, start when the creature enters combat. The aura moves with the creature and prompts eligible targets at the configured time. GMs can change its visibility or disable its recipe.

Supported Paladin auras share one attached Region that updates eligible allies’ benefits as they move into or out of range. See Paladin aura setup.

Combat Usage

Optional trackers show when a combatant has spent a Bonus Action or Reaction and clear those markers at the combatant’s next turn. The GM can clear a marker to allow an exception.

The Spell Slot Casting Tracker tracks slot-funded action and bonus-action spells for player characters during combat. It resets when the turn changes. Reaction spells spend their normal slot and Reaction independently of that tracker.

Legendary Actions

After a player’s turn, the combat tracker can remind the GM when an eligible monster has Legendary Action points available. The GM can use an action or advance to pass. The tracker skips the reminder when no eligible monster has points.
